Nov. 18, 1917 On leave 1918 Returned Aug. 30, 1918 5-192 BRIEF. APPLICATION OF Norman Bakke FOR THE ENROLLMENT OF Eleanor Gordon IN THE INDIAN SCHOOL AT Tacoma POST-OFFICE ADDRESS OF APPLICANT: South Bend Wash. Box 667. Date of enrollment, Nov. 18, 1917 Term of enrollment, Four (4) years. NAME OF PERSON ARRANGING FOR THE TRANSFER: Position, Reproduced at the National Archives at Seattle APPLICATION FOR ENROLLMENT IN A NONRESERVATION SCHOOL. (For a child not enrolled at an Agency.) For and in consideration of the United States assuming the care, education, and maintenance in the United States Indian school at Tacoma Washington, Eleanor Gordon, girl over 18 years old, of South Bend P.O., State of Washington, do hereby voluntarily consent and agree to enrollment in said school for a period of 4 years, and also obligate and bind myself to abide by all the rules and regulations for Indian schools. I further say that the said child was born at Hayward Wisconsin on March 31, 1910; that the father, Charles Gordon, is an Indian of the Chippawa Tribe located at Lee County Criello Agency; that he left the tribe about 1910; that the mother, Mabel Gordon, was White woman of the White Tribe located at Lee County Criello Agency, and left the tribe about 1910; that the said child was born and reared in the United States, and now actually resides therein; and that he has attended the following schools:
NAME OF SCHOOL—PUBLIC GOVERNMENT, OR MISSION. LOCATED AT— DATE OF ENROLLMENT. DATE OF DISCHARGE. CAUSE OF DISCHARGE. GRADE.
Public School South Bend Wash 1915 2nd
Should the child be returned home for one of the vacation periods of this enrollment at my request I further agree to pay all expenses, including round-trip railroad fares, sleeping-car fares, meals, lodging, stage fares, telegraph and telephone messages, and other incidental expenses connected with the visit. I further agree that pupil shall be returned to the school on or before the last day of the vacation leave of absence. I further agree to deposit with the superintendent of the school sufficient money to defray all expenses to be incurred, and should the child fail to return to school at such time and place as may be specified upon demand of the superintendent of the school, the amount of money remaining with the superintendent, necessary to the return transportation of the child so neglecting to return, shall be forfeited to the Government. This 15th day of November, 1917 Two witnesses: Oscar Hartman Mrs. Mary Lykensud (Parent, guardian, or next of kin) (NOTE.—Every blank in this application must be properly filled out by the applicant, in his own handwriting, if possible. The signature, whether by mark or otherwise, must be attested by two witnesses.) AFFIDAVIT. I, Norman Babbie, do hereby swear that the statements made in the above application are true. Sworn to and subscribed before me this 17th day of Nov. 1917. (signature of applicant) (Parent, guardian, or next of kin) (NOTE.—This application and affidavit must be executed before some officer authorized to administer oaths by the parent with whom the child is living; if the parent is dead, by the guardian or next of kin.) Tripp, a practicing physician of South Bend, Ind., do hereby certify that I have carefully examined Eleanor Gordon, the child named in this application, and find that she is in proper physical condition to attend school, and is not afflicted with tuberculosis or other disease which would be a menace to the health of other pupils. VOUCHERS OF DISINTERESTED PERSONS. Voucher No. 1 I, Oscar Hartman, a laborer of South Bend, do hereby certify that I am personally acquainted with Norman Babbie, who makes the foregoing application; that I believe his statements therein are true; that I am acquainted with Eleanor Gordon; that he is known and recognized in the community in which he lives as an Indian; that in my opinion he can not receive proper and adequate schooling at home for the reason that she has no Parents. Public school facilities: (Here state whether the child lives within reach of a public school, whether the State laws permit it to enroll therein, and if it lives near the public school why it can not attend such school.) Two near Public schools, but has no Parents to live with. This 15th day of Nov., 1917 Oscar Hartman VOUCHER NO. 2. I, Mrs. Harry L. Bale, a Housekeeper, of South Park, do hereby certify that I am personally acquainted with Norman Bailey, who makes the foregoing application; that I believe his statements therein are true; that I am acquainted with Eleanor Gordon; that he is known and recognized in the community in which he lives as an Indian; and that in my opinion he can not receive proper and adequate schooling at home for the reason that she has no parents. This 15 day of Nov., 1917 Mrs. Harry L. Bale CERTIFICATE OF SCHOOL PHYSICIAN. I hereby certify that on Sept. 1, 1917, I made a careful examination of the physical condition of Eleanor Gordon, the child named in the foregoing application, and found her to be in proper physical condition to attend School. I therefore recommend that the said child be enrolled in this school. This 19 day of Sept., 1919. Clement W. Turner, M.D. School Physician. The law provides: "That no part of this appropriation, or any other appropriation provided for herein except appropriations made pursuant to treaties, shall be used to educate children of less than one-fourth Indian blood whose parents are citizens of the United States and of the State wherein they live and where there are adequate free-school facilities provided and the facilities of the Indian schools are needed for pupils of more than one-fourth Indian blood." (Act of August 1, 1914.) EXTRACTS FROM SCHOOL RULES. If the facilities of a school are not needed as provided in the above paragraph, children showing any Indian blood, whose parents live on an Indian reservation, and who if debarred from Government schools could not obtain an education, may be enrolled in the day and boarding schools of their reservation; these children, however, may not be transferred to nonreservation schools without special permission from the Commissioner of Indian Affairs. Before enrolling a pupil superintendents must satisfy themselves whether he has left any other school without permission and whether he has been expelled for cause from any other school. A pupil who has been expelled for cause from any Indian school may be reenrolled in any Indian school only with permission of the Commissioner of Indian Affairs. "The Secretary of the Interior may in his discretion withhold rations, clothing, and other annuities from Indian parents or guardians who refuse to or neglect to send or keep their children of proper school age in some school during a reasonable portion of each year." (27 Stat. L., 635. See 2 Dec. Comp., 308.) Cushman Indian School, Tacoma, Wash. Nov. 2, 1918. Mr. Norman Bakke, South Bend, Washington. Dear Mr. Bakke: Eleanor Gordon was taken down with scarlet fever October 27th. At no time has she been seriously ill. Her temperature for several days has been normal, and we expect her to be well in due course of time. Her little uncle called to see her, but as she was quarantined, I could not permit it. You need not worry a moment about Eleanor. She will receive the best of care and attention. Sincerely yours, Superintendent N.B. November 5th. Eleanor is feeling nicely, and will soon be out.
